notes:
• Operator: checking off a to-do also archives its workspace when nothing is left in it. If a chat still works or asks, or there are uncommitted files or commits not pushed, you're asked first (Archive anyway / Keep workspace). The Operator can close workspaces too, with the same check, and only archives anyway with your OK.
• Operator: while the Operator works on a to-do itself (a check, a look-up), the to-do says so ("Operator · Checks the PR's CI"). It goes away when the to-do is done or the Operator stops.
• When Stellwerk isn't running on the Mac, the apps say so instead of "HTTP 502". A chat on the iPhone opens at its end. Every project with Entire shows its team chats block right away: a spinner while it loads, a refresh button when it's empty, and a failed load is retried after 10 seconds instead of a minute.
• Stellwerk for Mac: the host no longer stops answering when many git and command-line checks run at once, for example right after launch. Until now the Mac window, the phones and other Macs then couldn't reach it until Stellwerk was restarted.
• Mac: a file attached to your message opens in a tab next to the chats, like changed files. Images and videos open in a lightbox over the window that closes with Esc, instead of the Quick Look panel, which sometimes showed the wrong item and then stopped opening.
• Mac: buttons like "Continue in new workspace" get the same corners as Create PR instead of a capsule.
• Mac: the pointer turns into a hand over images and videos in the chat that open on click.
• Mac: filled buttons (Continue in new workspace, Restore, Clone, …) take the theme's colors like the send button instead of system blue.
• The Operator waits for a PR's checks: a chat that's done while its pull request's checks still run shows under "Checks running" (and in its to-do's line) instead of Ready, then moves to Ready when they pass or to Failed ("Checks failed.") when they don't. The Operator's status tool says so too. Mac, iOS and Android alike.
• The project setup says "Team chats for this project" and what you get (your team can read and continue the agents' chats) instead of "Enable Entire"; Entire is named as how it works.
